Based on the healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that pulmonary valve replacement is a procedure that may not be necessary or beneficial for some patients who have undergone repair of tetralogy of fallot. The consensus among the retrieved matches suggests that:

* Right ventricular recovery following PVR (pulmonary valve replacement) for chronic significant pulmonary regurgitation after repair of TOF (tetralogy of fallot) may be compromised in the adult population, indicating that patients should be considered before RV function deteriorates.
* Surgical procedures to prevent patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM) after aortic valve replacement are not justified in elderly patients aged at least 75 years, as PPM can affect survival and quality of life in these patients.
* Minimally invasive mitral valve repair with artificial chords is a safe and effective technique for routine cardiac surgery, especially when compared to traditional open-heart surgery.

Therefore, based on the available Q&A matches, it seems that operating too late for pulmonary valve replacement after tetralogy of fallot may not be justified. Patients should discuss their individual circumstances and risks with their healthcare provider before undergoing this procedure.
